# People API and access contract

All paths use `/api/v1`. Sessions require `X-Crew-Request: 1` for mutations. The canonical cookie is httpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Path=/; it also carries Secure when CREW_BASE_URL uses HTTPS. Signup/login issuance, logout, current-session revocation and password-reset clearing all use the same policy. The default local HTTP URL remains usable without Secure. Lists accept `limit` and `cursor` and return `items,nextCursor`.

`GET/POST /orgs` lists organizations for the signed-in account or creates one with `{name}`. Creation assigns its creator owner. `GET/PATCH /orgs/:orgId` reads or renames. `GET/POST /orgs/:orgId/members` lists or adds an existing account with `{userId,role}`. `PATCH/DELETE /orgs/:orgId/members/:userId` changes role or removes membership. At least one owner must remain; only owners appoint or manage owners. Removing membership also removes team memberships and project guest grants.

`GET/POST /orgs/:orgId/teams`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /teams/:teamId` use `{name,description}`. `GET/POST /teams/:teamId/members` and `DELETE /teams/:teamId/members/:userId` manage existing organization members. Duplicate names and memberships return 409.

Owners/admins administer organizations, people and projects. Members can read organizations and read/write project work. Guests can read their organization roster and teams, and only read/comment on specifically granted projects. Guest search/activity is restricted to those projects. `GET/POST /projects/:projectId/guests` and `DELETE /projects/:projectId/guests/:userId` require project administration. Post body is `{userId}` for an organization guest.

## Stable service for other lanes

People registers first. Use `ctx.permissions.assertOrg(req,orgId,permission='org:read')`, `assertProject(req,projectId,permission='project:read')`, `assertSelf(req,userId=req.user.id,permission='self:read')` and `scope(req,permission)`. Assertion methods throw stable AppErrors. `assertOrg` returns the membership; `assertProject` returns the raw project. `membership(userId,orgId)` returns a raw membership or null. `canOrg(userId,orgId,permission)` and `canProject(userId,projectId,permission)` return booleans; `projectIds(userId,orgId)` returns accessible project ids. Booleans do not check token scopes: route handlers must call `scope` as well. Projects have `projects.id,projects.org_id`; guests use people's `project_guests(project_id,user_id,created_at)`. Project deletion should remove guest rows.

Permission names: self:read/self:write, org:read/org:manage, members:manage, teams:manage, invites:manage, audit:read, project:read/project:write/project:manage, issue:write, comment:write, attachment:write, insight:read/insight:write, export:read, import:write. Tokens may name exact permissions, namespace wildcards such as project:*, or *. A scope never expands the user's role or project access.

## Shared outbox

One table `outbox(id,org_id,user_id,kind,to_email,subject,text_body,payload_json,created_at,sent_at)` stores invite/reset/digest rows. `org_id` and `user_id` may be null. Call `ctx.enqueueOutbox({orgId,userId,kind,toEmail,subject,textBody,payload})`, returning camelCase row metadata and parsed payload. Payloads for invite/reset contain the one-use link; digest payloads are insight-owned. This local outbox is the delivery surface; no external mail service is configured. Protect link contents as credentials. Do not create a second outbox table.

## Invitations and account security

`GET/POST /orgs/:orgId/invitations` requires invites:manage. POST accepts `{email,role,expiresInHours,projectIds}`. Expiry defaults to 168 hours, range 1–720. Only owners invite owners. Only guest invitations accept projectIds, all in the invitation organization. Pending duplicate invitations and existing memberships return 409. GET supports `state=pending|accepted|revoked|expired|all` before cursor pagination. `DELETE /invitations/:id` revokes a pending invitation. A revoked, accepted or expired link cannot be used again.

`POST /invitations/preview` accepts `{token}` and returns its pending recipient/organization/role. `POST /invitations/accept` requires self:write and the authenticated account's exact normalized email; it atomically adds the invited membership and guest project grants. The existing account's role cannot be overwritten. The link is delivered only to the single shared outbox; invitation responses expose metadata without credentials.

`GET /me/outbox?kind=invite|reset|digest` requires a browser session plus self:read and returns messages addressed to the current account only. Digest bodies, subjects and payload identifiers are reconstructed from current visible notifications; removed organization memberships hide their digest rows before pagination. `GET /orgs/:orgId/outbox` requires invites:manage and exposes that organization's invitation messages only. Treat outbox link text/payload as private credentials. No external email delivery is configured.

`GET /auth/sessions` requires self:read and lists unexpired sessions with current, lastUsedAt, expiresAt and userAgent metadata. `DELETE /auth/sessions/:id` requires self:write and revokes only a session owned by the caller; deleting the current one clears its cookie. `POST /auth/sessions/revoke-others` with `{}` revokes all other sessions.

`POST /auth/password/change` takes `{currentPassword,password}` and requires self:write, verifies the existing scrypt hash, retains the current browser session, and revokes every other session, personal API token and outstanding reset link. API-token callers must sign in again afterwards. New passwords require 10–1024 characters and must differ from the current password.

`POST /auth/password/reset/request` accepts `{email}` and always returns the same 202 response for known/unknown valid addresses. Known accounts receive a one-hour link through the shared outbox; a new request invalidates older links. `POST /auth/password/reset` accepts `{token,password}`. It is public, uses the one-use link, and revokes all sessions and API tokens. Sign in again after reset. Invalid, expired and used links return 422; concurrent consumption returns 409. An administrator operating this local diagnostic service can retrieve a reset message from private runtime data when the account has no active session.

Sessions, invite/reset links and personal API tokens use random 256-bit credentials signed with CREW_SECRET using HMAC-SHA256 and distinct purpose tags. Database lookup stores SHA256 only. Verification requires the exact canonical unpadded base64url encoding of both the 32-byte nonce and signature, checks purpose/signature before lookup, and rejects alternate spellings with changed unused encoding bits. Changing CREW_SECRET invalidates existing credentials. Keep CREW_SECRET stable across restarts and restore it alongside the private data backup. Outbox intentionally stores delivery links until an operator removes private runtime data. Password hashes, link credentials and plaintext tokens never enter domain events or audit summaries.

## Personal API tokens and security audit

`POST /tokens` accepts `{name,scopes,expiresInDays}` and requires self:write. Name is at most 100 characters. Choose exact permissions, known namespace wildcards or `*`; expiry is 1–365 days or null for no expiry. Defaults grant self:read, org:read, project:read and insight:read. Creation returns `{personalToken,token}`; save the plaintext token then, because GET never repeats it. Tokens store only SHA256 lookup hashes. A token may mint only a subset of its own scopes. `GET /tokens?state=all|active|expired|revoked` requires self:read and returns metadata/scopes/state/lastUsedAt. `DELETE /tokens/:id` requires self:write and revokes a caller-owned token immediately. Expired/revoked/signed-with-another-secret tokens return 401. An invalid Bearer credential never falls back to a cookie.

`ctx.authenticateToken(plaintext)` returns `{kind:'token',tokenId,user,scopes}` after signature, hash, expiry and revoke checks. Authentication uses the same users, sessions, publicUser and hashToken helpers as browser login. Every subsequent handler must check both scope and current role/project access; a wildcard cannot make a guest an administrator. Account outbox links require browser authentication even if a token has self:read. Organization invitation outbox access requires invites:manage.

`GET /orgs/:orgId/audit` requires audit:read and administrator/owner membership. Filters are actorId, entityType, entityId, projectId, action, from and to (inclusive ISO timestamps), plus limit/cursor. Cross-organization project filters are rejected. `GET /me/audit` requires self:read and returns only the account's own security actions with no organization context. Persisted security types include organization/membership, team/roster, invitation, session, user login/password/reset and personal token creation/revocation; project guest grants are included. Summaries allow only explicit identity/role/scope/lifecycle fields. No arbitrary request, password hash, token hash, plaintext token or delivery payload is persisted into audit. The audit event subscriber is removed during ctx.cleanup before server drain.

## Administration web and CLI

Organizations, member rosters, teams and team rosters offer opaque-cursor Next/Previous pages; the team member picker also browses the complete roster. Destructive membership/team/invite/session/token controls require deliberate confirmation. Forms retain input on errors and show field details. Organization tabs open Members, Teams, Invitations and Audit. Account security opens Sessions/Password, Tokens, personal Audit and Outbox. Token creation shows a private copy-once credential with an explicit hide action. Invitation pages distinguish pending/expired/revoked/accepted; accepted/reset links cannot be replayed.

Use `crew org --help`, `crew team --help`, `crew invite --help` and `crew token --help` for full commands and options. `org` supports list/show/create/rename/members/add/role/remove, guest project grants and filtered audit. `team` supports list/show/create/update/delete/members/add/remove. `invite` supports list/create/preview/accept/revoke/outbox. `token` supports list/create/revoke. Lists preserve items/nextCursor and support --limit/--cursor. Destructive commands require --yes. `invite accept --link URL` requires the invited account; --credential supplies the token directly when needed. `token create --name TOOL --scopes self:read,org:read --days 30 --save-to FILE` writes a private 0600 CLI config containing the token; without --save-to creation prints it once. `CREW_TOKEN` or --token uses Bearer authentication; --config selects a stored config. Do not put secrets in command history on a shared machine.

People data persists in `CREW_DATA_DIR/crew.sqlite` alongside the shared outbox and sanitized audit. Attachment bytes remain in the work-owned attachments directory. Stop Crew and back up the entire data directory plus CREW_SECRET configuration; restore both together. CLI configuration defaults to ~/.config/crew/config.json and is private. Acceptance credentials/configs live only under private data/ and are excluded from production source.

## Current route audit boundary

The final people.5 review covers the 119 currently registered API method/path pairs: six explicit public health/auth/link entrypoints and 113 authenticated routes. `scripts/checks/people.mjs` discovers registration from the actual application and sends unauthenticated HTTP requests to every protected route. This census complements the source review and role/scope/ownership tests; a 401 census alone does not prove authorized behavior.

The reviewed boundary includes canonical session/token authentication, auth and people administration, project/workflow management, issue/label/comment/relation mutations and revision conflicts, board/bulk changes, sprint scope/candidate/carry-target selectors, attachments, search/catalog/suggestions, saved personal/team filters and execution, activity/feed, subscriptions, inbox/bulk marking/preferences, digests, entity options, dashboards, JSON/CSV export, import preview/publication, and live SSE. Every protected operation uses the existing permission service. Boolean membership/project helpers remain scope-independent, so handlers explicitly assert the operation's token scope. Scope does not replace current role, organization membership, project grants, private ownership or team membership.

Search candidates are restricted to accessible project documents before matching, ranking, highlighting, facets and pagination. Feeds, notification counts, digest items, dashboard data, selectors and exports apply current access before pagination or delivery. Relation visibility requires both endpoints; export external endpoints and import remaps must stay within authorized projects and destinations. Import requires import:write, project:manage, issue:write and comment:write, including preview. Personal filters and inbox records cannot be read or changed by another account; team sharing requires membership in the same organization and team. Work candidate reads and mutations check project access before returning choices or revision-conflict snapshots.

Both `GET /digests` and browser-only `GET /me/outbox?kind=digest` use the same current-visible digest renderer. Revoking a project grant removes its notification identifiers, body lines and count from both surfaces; removing organization membership omits that organization's delivery row before pagination. The private outbox reconstructs the digest subject and payload from visible items. Stored delivery history remains in SQLite and is not deleted or treated as current authorization. Invitation/reset links retain exact recipient ownership and browser-session-only access. The organization outbox exposes invitations only; general activity, SSE and digest views exclude credential links.

SSE authenticates again and rechecks token scope, organization membership and project access for each event and heartbeat. Revoked sessions/tokens and removed selected memberships/grants close the stream before further delivery. Disconnect and application cleanup release subscriptions; slow clients are closed when the response cannot accept a frame. Web callers show access errors, clear failed search results, keep scoped loads separate, and expose explicit live pause/resume controls. Saved-filter edits retain the local draft after denial and offer deliberate latest-version inspection after conflicts. Import previews and mapping decisions require explicit confirmation before publication. Previously delivered browser data cannot be remotely erased by a later revocation; every subsequent HTTP request and live delivery still checks current authority.

`packages/server/test/people-delivery.test.js`, `people-integration.test.js` and the integrated insight/work suites cover positive access, attenuated tokens, guest grants, private state, cross-organization targets and cleanup through real HTTP. `packages/cli/test/people-boundaries.test.js` exercises actual CLI scope denials, guest filtering, denied-export file cleanup, import-preview denial and immediate revoked-token denial. `insight-sse.test.js` proves live session/token/grant/membership revocation and listener cleanup. These are final integration checks for this reviewed source; any later registered route or changed access path needs review and relevant proof at its new source identity.


## Member access administration and explicit role decisions (P1e)

Owners and administrators open **Manage access** from the organization member list.
The dedicated member page separates effective role-derived project access from stored
direct grants. A direct grant survives promotion to member/admin/owner as a dormant
record. A later downgrade to guest makes only the retained direct grants effective.
Removing a dormant grant changes future guest access and leaves current role access
intact. Adding a new direct grant requires the target's current guest membership.
Archived projects remain visible and labeled; their archived product behavior remains
read-only. Membership removal retains the existing removal of teams and direct grants.

- `GET /orgs/:orgId/members/:userId/access` requires `members:manage` and
  `project:manage` token scopes plus current owner/admin role. It returns the exact
  same-organization membership, actor role, project/direct/archived counts and a
  read-only role capability/access-impact matrix derived from canonical `roleAllows`.
  `lastOwner`, `canChangeRole` and per-role `selectable` are presentation guidance;
  the canonical mutation always rechecks current owner/target/last-owner authority.
- `GET /orgs/:orgId/members/:userId/projects` has the same authority. It supports
  `q`, `mode=all|direct`, exact selected `id`, `limit` (1–200) and cursor. The SQL
  window returns at most limit+1 rows and counts/searches only the authorized
  organization. The cursor is bound to organization, target, search, mode and selected
  id. A foreign selected project resolves to an empty list. Each result includes full
  key/name, `archived`, `grantedAt`, `direct`, `dormant` and canonical current
  `effective` project visibility. There is no 200-project total cap or eager client
  materialization. Search/page actions leave saved grants unchanged.
- Existing `POST /projects/:projectId/guests` and
  `DELETE /projects/:projectId/guests/:userId` remain the only direct-grant mutations.
  Their current `project:manage`, organization membership and guest-target checks
  apply. The web shows the selected person's and project's labels in confirmation.
- The role selector changes a local proposal only. **Review role change** displays
  before/after permissions, accessible project counts, dormant grants and access loss.
  **Confirm role change** re-reads that exact access summary and refuses a changed
  preview before using the existing membership PATCH with `expectedRevision`.
  Direct grants are never automatically added or removed by this flow.

## Administration draft and request ownership (P1e)

Organization and team public records now include `revision`, the same canonical
SHA-256 record hash used by work mutations. Their existing PATCH bodies optionally
accept `expectedRevision`; existing clients without it retain their existing API.
The revision excludes its own field and is content-based, so equal timestamps do not
conceal independent changes. A stale authorized mutation returns 409 with a current
snapshot and changes no record or domain/audit event. Authorization precedes snapshot
construction. Membership role PATCH also accepts the optional current roster revision.
The pure helper is now `server/src/http/revisions.js`; the work path re-exports the
same functions and retains all existing work callers and semantics.

Dirty organization/team drafts survive canonical refresh, conflict and access loss.
**Inspect latest version** reads current authorized state. **Load latest version**
requires an explicit replacement decision. **Keep my changes on latest version**
preserves independent newer fields; overlapping fields require mine/latest choices.
Applying choices updates the local draft and revision; Save remains a separate action
and a later peer change can still conflict. Access loss leaves a disabled retained
local draft visible, with no current snapshot delivered by the denied server request.
Local draft custody lasts for the current mounted page; leaving/reloading the document
is not a persistent draft-storage feature.

People actions reuse the existing work planning lifetime. One synchronous owner rejects
a duplicate pending submit, passes `AbortSignal` to HTTP and runs store/navigation and
other completion callbacks only for the current page/resource/query/opaque link owner.
Resource change and unmount abort local waiting and suppress abandoned success/error/
completion state. Cancellation does not promise to roll back a server-accepted change;
refresh current state before making a new decision. Paging reuses the insight scoped
load projection, starts a changed path/search at cursor null on its first render, and
withholds another scope's data during loading/error. No request is automatically replayed.

## Audit choices and field-level review (P1e)

`GET /orgs/:orgId/audit-options` shares canonical organization `audit:read` scope and
role authority with audit queries. `GET /me/audit-options` shares the existing exact
account `self:read` authority. Both accept `type=actors|targets|actions|projects`,
`q`, exact selected `id`, optional target `entityType`, `limit` and cursor. They derive
all option identities, labels and counts from the same already-authorized sanitized
audit events. They do not query a separate user/project directory or grant unrelated
member/project scopes. Names are used only where a safe name exists in those events;
otherwise a readable recorded-type/id suffix identifies a historical target/actor.
Removed identities can remain as recorded historical audit choices. Other-organization
and other-account identities have no selected resolution. These are bounded response
choices over the existing canonical audit projection, not a new audit/search index.

An `audit:read`-only organization token may filter an authorized project audit without
also gaining `project:read` API or `org:read`/member API scopes. Current canonical
project visibility and exact organization are checked for that filter. Foreign project
filters fail validation. Ordinary project/member routes retain their own token scopes.

The page separates draft versus applied filters, preserves applied cursor identity,
resolves selected labels on later option pages, and requires exact UTC `...Z` time
inputs. Details show only changed safe fields in Before/After columns, distinguishing
absent, cleared and empty values. Changing scope/filter/page or losing access closes
old detail delivery; failed loads expose no previous results. Existing audit sanitizing
continues excluding credentials, password hashes and invitation/reset links.

Qualification is recorded in `server/test/people-admin.test.js`,
`web/test/people-admin-state.test.js` and the real pinned Chromium
`web/test/people-admin-browser.test.js` scenarios. Earlier P1d's 119-route evidence
is historical and does not qualify the four P1e routes. The final runtime census proves
registration and anonymous denial; dedicated role/scoped/current-resource tests supply
positive and negative authority coverage. Whole-application acceptance and publication
remain the lead's responsibility.
